title: SIP caller through explicit interpreter to WebRTC T.140 boundary
objective: Prove the open federation boundary in stages: a live SIP dialog reaches an explicit interpreter participant, the interpreter is independently readiness-gated, and the destination-facing boundary preserves the RFC 8865 T.140 data-channel profile without treating a reference boundary as a real browser implementation.

execution.sipLeftBoundary: existing JAIN SIP BaudotProbe caller/callee harness with the callee interpreted as the explicit interpreter participant
execution.browserRightBoundary: baudot_reference RFC 8865 profile and T.140 message parser

runnableEvidence: live JAIN SIP dialog establishment is available independently of browser-boundary reduction
interpreter readiness remains a separate terminal fact from SIP establishment
destination-facing T.140 content is parsed through the RFC 8865 reference boundary
the t140/reliable/ordered data-channel profile is checked independently of provider identity
wrong profile and invalid UTF-8 remain distinguishable from SIP or interpreter failure
requiredBeforeProven: one repeatable run with a real browser RTCPeerConnection
SCTP data-channel establishment observed in the browser implementation
DTLS and ICE state preserved as evidence rather than inferred from application success
subprotocol t140 observed from the live browser data channel
first browser-originated or browser-received T.140 user message preserved and independently parsed
same terminal reducer exercised without provider-specific branches

doesNotEstablish: that the reference right boundary is a browser
